study: One participant sub-04, four physical EEG observations. Generic known-object feasibility only. Earlier research used these 96 objects for different attributes. No target panel or cloud job.
measurement: Use original author's indexed crop512 distinct photos; U2NetP fixed normalized soft mask, take <=0.10, erode by a 9x9 square at 320 and sample at 160. Require at least 15% of pixels. sRGB luma coefficients .2126,.7152,.0722; light neutral means luma>=.75 and pixel max-min<=.20. Background population SD and fraction of valid horizontal/vertical adjacent pairs at 160 with absolute luma difference>=.06. Positive (clean light) requires light-neutral coverage>=.75, SD<=.12, edge rate<=.12. Negative (varied setting) requires coverage<=.40 and either SD>=.16 or edge rate>=.15. All others uncertain. Report each label and valid/missing fractions; no claiming semantic scene recognition.
training: Map confident positive/negative and uncertain to 1/0/.5. Within training object center both X and Y across its 10 photos. Physical R4 mean of 17 posterior channels in 20ms bins 60-460ms (340 predictors). Divide X by train SD (floor 1e-6). Ridge .3 times number of images. For each test fold hold adjacent photo pair by original ordinal, compute query and label baseline relative only to the other 8 supports. The supported object is supplied in this generic experiment. No query image/label enters prediction. Prior mean of 8 codes. Compute raw EEG increment plus separately a nuisance-only increment by learning X to 4 appearance features (whole crop mean RGB and luma SD), followed by within-object standardized nuisance-to-Y ridge .05*n trained on 320. Both predictions use EEG+support only. Held 96 calibration objects (disjoint from fit and evaluation) fit just one scalar each (correct residual LS, clipped [0,2]) to map increments to probabilities; use all codes on calibration including neutral .5. Clip all probabilities to [.01,.99]. Wrong EEG exchanges the other held photo in the same true/assumed word and fold.
evaluation: Blind inference reads eight support annotation codes per active fold only; evaluation reads query labels afterwards. Primary Brier benefits on confidently annotated photos: compare matched EEG against eight-support prior, wrong EEG, and EEG-estimated nuisance-only control. Report raw/adjusted accuracy, empirical annotation and reliable-choice rates, uncertain rows, pooled and class-cluster intervals. Independent nonoverlapping adjacent pairs where one label is clean and other textured: matched EEG assigns higher score to clean (ties half). Strict confident labels alone enter primary endpoint. Report comparator pair metrics and group counts, and diagnostic on all codes; actual target photometry is never available to the decoder.
policy: Emit 'against a plain, light-colored background' if p>=.75 and EEG increases eight-support probability by >=.10. Emit 'with a visibly varied, textured background' if p<=.25 and EEG decreases it by >=.10. Otherwise leave the original object prompt. Emit only after passing primary gate. Report attempted actions, correctness vs measured labels, confidence intervals and uncertain labels. Examples fixed as first two by original ID for each action plus first two by each true annotation, private only originals.
gate: Across 96 evaluation objects, paired whole-object bootstrap lower 95% >0 for Brier benefit over prior, swapped EEG and nuisance-only. Opposite-label disjoint-pair assignment lower 95% >.5 and at least 20 such pairs; at least 20 actionable confident photos with point precision >=.70. All must hold. Do not create target rendering packet otherwise. Bootstrap 10000 same whole-object draws, seed 260701; use ratio of pooled totals per draw; skip empty resamples.
